messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the test sets up:
  - initializeTestData() compresses TEXT using BZip2 and then truncates the last 10 bytes, specifically removing the end-of-stream marker (eos_magic, 6 bytes) and the final CRC (4 bytes). This leaves the actual compressed blocks intact but removes the trailer at the very end.
  - initializeChannel() wraps this truncated byte array in a BZip2CompressorInputStream and exposes it through a ReadableByteChannel.
- What the CPython test expects (and documents in comments in the test):
  - Reading exactly len(TEXT) bytes should succeed and return the full TEXT, because the data blocks themselves are complete; only the trailer is missing.
  - A subsequent read (e.g., 1 extra byte) should detect the missing trailer and raise EOFError/IOException.
- What happens in Commons Compress:
  - PythonTruncatedBzip2Test.testPartialReadTruncatedData() allocates a ByteBuffer of size TEXT.length() and performs a single read: bz2Channel.read(buffer).
  - The channel delegates to BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], off, len). That method loops calling read0() until it has produced len bytes or until read0() returns -1 (EOF).
    - See BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], int, int) lines 174–181:
      - It will stop early and return the number of bytes read so far if read0() returns -1 at any point in the loop.
    - read0() returns -1 when the decompressor’s currentState is EOF (lines 200–203).
  - The decompressor’s state machine (the setupNoRandPartB/C and related methods invoked by read0()) attempts to transition at block boundaries and validate what follows. Because the eos_magic + CRC have been removed, the end-of-stream validation fails once the last block is finished and the implementation tries to consume/validate the trailer.
  - In the current implementation, this “end-of-stream is missing” condition causes the state to move to EOF (so read0() returns -1) within the same top-level read(byte[], off, len) call. As soon as read0() returns -1, read(byte[], ...) stops and returns the number of bytes already produced, which is less than the requested len(TEXT).
- Why this diverges from CPython and causes the test failure:
  - CPython’s bz2 implementation completes decoding of all available data blocks and only raises an error (EOFError) when the caller tries to read past the last decoded byte—i.e., when the trailer is actually needed. Thus, a single read of len(TEXT) yields the full TEXT.
  - Commons Compress, by contrast, signals EOF (via currentState == EOF causing read0() == -1) before fulfilling the requested number of bytes in the same read call once it detects the missing trailer. This results in a short read (fewer bytes than len(TEXT)) rather than returning the complete TEXT.
  - This behavior is reflected by the loop in read(byte[], off, len): it terminates early as soon as read0() reports EOF, returning a count smaller than len, which is exactly what the failing test is observing.
- Summary of root cause:
  - Trailer verification (eos_magic + final CRC) is performed and reacted to too early with respect to the contract expected by the test. The state machine transitions to EOF (or otherwise stops producing bytes) during the same read call that should still be delivering the last bytes of the final block, causing a partial read. CPython defers error reporting until the next read past the end; Commons Compress currently ends the read early when it hits the truncated trailer.
  - The result is that BZip2CompressorInputStream returns fewer bytes from a truncated stream than CPython’s bz2 does for the same read length, breaking the shared regression test.
